transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Please have a seat. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I've been struggling with eating extremely large amounts of food. Once I start, I feel like I completely lose control and just can't stop myself.
How often do these episodes happen, and do they cause you significant distress?

They happen at least once a week on average, and this has been going on for about a year now. It definitely causes me a lot of distress, especially because I feel so embarrassed and completely out of control when it happens.
During these episodes, do you eat much more rapidly than normal, eat until you're uncomfortably full, or eat large amounts when not physically hungry?
I definitely eat huge amounts of food even when I'm not physically hungry at all. As for eating too fast or until I'm uncomfortably full, I don't really notice or experience those things as much.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "binge-eating associated behaviors",
  "question": "Do you ever make yourself vomit, misuse laxatives, or engage in extreme exercise or fasting because of these eating episodes?"
No, I don't do any of those things. I have never tried to make myself throw up, use laxatives, or fast to make up for what I ate.

The patient reports recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food despite not being physically hungry, experiencing a sense of loss of control, and significant distress. The absence of compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise rules out Bulimia Nervosa. No other symptoms suggesting alternative diagnoses (e.g., mood, anxiety, or psychotic disorders) have been reported. Criteria for Binge-Eating Disorder are met.
